description: JavaScript Object Notation is a lightweight, human-readable text format for exchanging structured data as key-value pairs and arrays
YAML Ain't Markup Language is a human-readable data serialization format based on indentation, often used for configuration files
Portable Document Format is an ISO standard for fixed-layout documents; data usually has to be extracted from text or tables for import
Markdown is a lightweight markup language with plain-text formatting syntax that stays readable as-is; headings, lists and tables can be parsed for import
Plain text is unstructured or loosely structured text without markup; values have to be identified by parsing or manual review
Tom's Obvious Minimal Language is a minimal configuration file format with explicit typing that maps unambiguously to a hash table
eXtensible Markup Language is a W3C standard text format for storing and exchanging hierarchically structured data using self-describing tags
eXtensible Business Reporting Language is a freely available global framework for exchanging business information
Comma-Separated Values is a simple plain-text format for tabular data where each line is a row and values are separated by a delimiter
Tab-Separated Values is a plain-text format for tabular data like CSV, but uses tab characters as delimiters, which avoids most quoting problems
Office Open XML Spreadsheet is the ISO/IEC 29500 standard spreadsheet format used by Microsoft Excel, stored as zipped XML files
OpenDocument Spreadsheet is the ISO/IEC 26300 open standard spreadsheet format used by LibreOffice Calc and other office suites
An Application Programming Interface is a machine-readable web service endpoint that delivers data on request, often as JSON or XML
Open Data Protocol is an OASIS standard for REST APIs that allows querying and filtering of data through standardized URL conventions
JSON for Linked Data is a W3C standard for encoding linked data in JSON, so that RDF triples can be exchanged in a web-developer-friendly format
Resource Description Framework is a W3C standard for describing linked data as subject-predicate-object triples, serialized for example as Turtle or RDF/XML
SPARQL Protocol and RDF Query Language endpoint is a W3C standard query service for retrieving linked data from triple stores such as Wikidata
Statistical Data and Metadata eXchange is an ISO standard used by statistical offices and central banks to exchange time series and their metadata
JSON-stat is a lightweight JSON format for multidimensional statistical tables, used by several national statistical offices
GeoJSON is a JSON-based format (RFC 7946) for encoding geographic features such as points, lines and polygons with their properties
Apache Parquet is an open columnar binary storage format optimized for efficient compression and fast analytical queries on large datasets
Apache Avro is a row-based binary serialization format with an embedded JSON schema, often used for data streams and schema evolution
Network Common Data Form is a self-describing binary format for multidimensional array data, widely used in climate and earth sciences
Hierarchical Data Format version 5 is a binary format for storing large, complex scientific datasets in a file-system-like hierarchy
Structured Query Language dump is a text file of SQL statements that recreates database tables and their content when executed
HyperText Markup Language is the standard markup language of web pages; data is usually extracted from tables or structured elements by scraping
SQLite is a self-contained serverless relational database engine that stores an entire database, including tables and indexes, in a single file
Web ARChive is a standardized file format for storing web content together with metadata from web crawling and archiving
Really Simple Syndication is an XML-based format for distributing frequently updated web content such as news articles and feeds
Atom is an XML-based web syndication format and protocol for distributing periodically updated content
Turtle is a compact, human-readable RDF serialization format using prefixes and subject-predicate-object statements
N-Triples is a simple line-based RDF serialization in which each line represents one subject-predicate-object triple
